expectation: The real app window opens and the bridge reports StationAI API version 1.
Blank titles, missing roots, unavailable roots, and nonexistent merge targets cannot create a task.
Creating a repository task persists its selected branch settings as pending, shows auto when no branch is chosen, and creates no Git branch or worktree until the first conversation send.
A selected existing branch remains pending until task start, then reuses its exact existing worktree path.
Selecting multiple repositories persists pending auto branch records without creating branches or worktrees before the task starts.
A folder-only task persists its context without Git worktrees and reaches Done after a successful turn without attempting a merge.
A worktree already assigned to another active task is rejected without creating another task.

After a successful Codex turn puts a task with no changes in Review, the merge target advances before Done, and dropping the task on Done preserves the newer target commit without an empty squash commit, removes the clean managed worktree, retains the source branch and conversation history, persists the submitted conversation prompt, reduces the active task count, and exposes the task in the searchable archive with case-insensitive search and a read-only conversation.
Moving a reviewed task to Done stages and commits tracked and untracked worktree changes, squash-merges them into the target as a single-parent commit, and removes the managed worktree.
A dirty local merge target is detected before the merge, leaves the target unchanged, moves the reviewed task to Blocked with the reason, and keeps it out of the Done archive.
A missing explicit local merge target leaves the branch unmerged and moves the reviewed task to Blocked with the reason.

A later repository squash-commit failure preserves the earlier completed merge and leaves the failed target unchanged and clean; after retry, StationAI skips the completed merge and finishes the remaining repository.
An active conflict-resolution turn remains In Progress when read, leaves the target branch unchanged, and returns the task to Review; a second Done request merges it.
The one-time lifecycle rollout clears task records and clean managed worktrees, preserves branches, and retains dirty managed worktrees with a notice.

The board keeps stacked Blocked/Backlog and conditional Waiting Response/In Progress sections fully visible, leaves Review as its own column, removes Done from the columns, hides empty status sections, and preserves Codex-owned task status behavior.

The CLI publishes standard and custom progress only during an active task turn, persists each report across fresh CLI/XPC connections, rejects invalid reports, clears explicitly and at turn completion, and the board card shows the built-in icon, label, and detail without changing lifecycle status; each turn receives hidden CLI usage instructions.

Progress reports clear when turns fail or are interrupted and when Codex requests user input; the task card removes the report while lifecycle states remain Blocked or Waiting Response, and answering the question resumes the task successfully.
A rename persists; rejecting a blank rename preserves the last valid title.
Root editing preserves order, removes duplicates, and rejects an empty list.

Repository suggestions can be filtered and navigated with Up/Down, and Enter selects the highlighted repository; adding it persists a pending auto branch with labeled read-only branch, merge-from, and merge-to values, and no worktree exists before the first send.

The task context menu offers deletion. Pending repository tasks delete without confirmation and preserve the source repository; clean started worktrees can be deleted; dirty started worktrees require confirmation, and canceling preserves the task and worktree. CLI delete-check reports the confirmation requirement, confirmed deletion removes the managed worktree, and the persistent log captures a real deletion failure's task, thread, process, phase, underlying error details, and no task title or conversation text; the failed task and worktree remain available for retry.

The default parent can be read, changed, cleared, and an unavailable path is rejected; the ordered last-used repository list persists across fresh CLI/XPC connections and rejects unavailable repositories; Dark and Light appearance choices persist, and Dark renders the workspace canvas as #1E1E1E in the VS Code Dark+ palette.

Suggestions include top-level Git roots and skip nested repositories and symlink targets; the picker placeholder shows saved repositories with a Return arrow, and blank Return reuses them in order, while typing and arrow-key selection overrides that default, which persists after task creation.
Clearing the default parent does not change roots already saved on a task.

Creating a task opens its empty conversation with the repository picker search focused and shows Untitled task until a first prompt starts title generation; the task has no stored messages or activity, and backing out immediately deletes it without a confirmation.

Creating a repository task leaves its selected branch pending while backing out saves an unsent prompt; reopening restores the draft without creating a branch or worktree, and invalid status changes are rejected without mutation.

Shift+Enter inserts a newline in the composer without sending; multiline prompts persist as typed text, blank drafts cannot be sent or stored, sent prompts persist in conversation history through reload, and sending to an Untitled task persists either the Codex-generated title or a prompt-based fallback when title generation fails.

The conversation composer accepts images from the picker and paste, previews them before sending, sends image-only or text-and-image prompts to Codex using the tagged image URL payload, and displays attached images from reloaded conversation history.
Malformed image data is rejected with a visible composer error and an invalid_argument bridge response, without creating conversation history or advancing task status.
When Codex delegates a task to a subagent, the conversation activity shows the delegated task and its completion status during the turn and after history reload.
Selecting Plan mode sends a planning turn; Markdown headings and lists render as distinct conversation elements after reopening, and bridge history preserves the assistant's exact Markdown source.
The composer shows a Codex-reported model, while unsupported modes and malformed model IDs are rejected before creating history.

Structured questions raised in Plan mode move the task into the conditional Waiting Response board section even when Codex marks the request non-blocking; reopening preserves its status, keyed answers resume In Progress, and successful completion moves it to Review.
Non-blocking structured questions remain visible without moving the task out of In Progress, then successful completion moves it to Review.

Turn start persists In Progress; reopening while a turn is still active recovers the stale task to Blocked with a reason. Interrupted outcomes also persist Blocked across connections, and a new prompt can finish in Review.

A failed turn preserves its blocked reason and appears in the compact Blocked section above Backlog with a user-intervention indication; retrying clears that section and completes the task into Review.
The task view separates staged and working Git changes, and selecting text or JSON files opens a calculated, highlighted side-by-side diff over the conversation.
External file edits and Git commits update the open task's changes sidebar automatically, and fresh CLI connections report the same Git status.
